rv.q: “The Sound Inside” aspires toward elegiac, literary meditation on mortality but delivers mostly pretentious banalities.
Her portrayal is captivating, seeping into the cracks and shadows of the story to come out shining.
Falls couldn't have selected a better play to begin his theatre's three-show foray into live-but-remote stagings.
The expertly paced, evolving drama is a stunning reminder of the power of live theatre.
“The Sound Inside” will echo loudly in your consciousness for a long time to come.
The stunning ending, which blends fiction, grief and friendship, speaks to us in this pandemic year.

“The Sound Inside,” by Adam Rapp, the Jefferson Award winning and Pulitzer Prize nominated playwright of “Red Light Winter,” is a perfect choice for Goodman Theatre’s first live performance on its Owen Theatre stage.

cn.t: Critics are divided on Adam Rapp's psychological drama, with most praising the polished production and performances while one finds the script overwrought. The Goodman's return to live theater earns enthusiasm.
